sovereign_country.strategic_role: 支持全中文章程、传统华人客群离岸家族信托常驻地

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Digital Magazine Publishing and Sponsored Media Placements

meta_jurisdiction_context.sovereign_country_en: Independent State of Samoa (Malo Sa'oloto Tuto'atasi o Samoa)
meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa — International Company (IC) regime administered by the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law foundation, local statutory enactments, and Fa'asamoa customary law elements)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: PACER Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus; in force 13 December 2020; regional trade and investment framework with Australia, New Zealand and Pacific Forum states)
SPARTECA (South Pacific Regional Trade and Economic Co-operation Agreement; preferential trade framework with Australia and New Zealand)
WTO Membership (Samoa acceded 10 May 2012; GATS and TRIPS commitments relevant to cross-border digital publishing)

Note: no active comprehensive Samoan double-taxation agreement or bilateral investment treaty conferring treaty benefits on an International Company was identified; the IC's Samoan tax exemption is sourced in domestic statute and does not require treaty reliance

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 2017 (No. 3 of 2017), as amended, and International Companies Regulations 2018 (name reservation, registered agent, registered office, registers, confidentiality, and economic substance); Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2018 and Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Regulations 2018 (customer due diligence, beneficial owner identification, PEP and sanctions requirements); SIFA AML/CFT Compliance Rules and circulars; Central Bank of Samoa KYC directives; Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (Samoa FIU) reporting obligations. Nominee arrangements remain lawful but must be documented through an SIFA-licensed service provider, and the underlying beneficial owner must be disclosed to the registered agent and, on demand, to the Registrar, SIFA and Samoa FIU; UBO piercing is therefore resolved through the licensed agent's CDD file rather than through any public register.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) — Registrar of International Companies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Samoa Competent Authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade; Apostille Convention in force for Samoa) OR consular legalization at a Samoan Embassy or Permanent Mission for non-Apostille states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of No Current Liabilities)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade OR consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (notarized; may include a bilingual English-Chinese text and a parallel Chinese-character trade denomination)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public admitted in Samoa, countersigned by the licensed registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille OR consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified register of directors, shareholders and beneficial owners (sealed extract prepared by the registered agent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille OR consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based client due diligence before incorporation: (i) identity verification and UBO tracing of every natural person owning or controlling 25% or more of shares or voting rights, or otherwise exercising control through nominee or trust chains; (ii) mandatory screening against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Samoa FIU domestic designations and Interpol notices; (iii) PEP determination under the AML/CFT Act 2018 with enhanced due diligence for foreign and domestic PEPs, family members and close associates; (iv) negative media and adverse-information checks; (v) source-of-funds and source-of-wealth analysis; and (vi) ongoing transaction monitoring and STR reporting to the Samoa FIU upon suspicion or at prescribed thresholds. For this digital magazine publishing and sponsored-media scope, the residual AML risk tier is Low_Risk_Standard.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority — International Companies Registry; applications are lodged by an SIFA-licensed registered agent through SIFA's official channel (www.sifa.gov.ws) or physically at the SIFA office, Matafele, Apia. Domestic (non-IC) company names are filed separately with the Companies Registry of the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory registered name must be in Latin/Roman script and must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd'. SIFA registry practice permits (i) a parallel Chinese-character or other foreign-script trade denomination recorded in the Memorandum and Articles, and (ii) bilingual Chinese-English constitutional documents, provided the English text governs and the foreign-script name is a faithful transliteration or translation of the English name; the foreign-script name may not alone constitute the registered name, and must not introduce any prohibited or sensitive token (including banking, trust, insurance or state-patronage words in translation). All official certificates, registers and registry extracts are issued in English.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Government, Crown, Royal, Imperial, State, Ministry, Municipality, Samoa Government, Western Samoa — presumed to imply patronage of the Samoan State; prohibited absent ministerial consent
Samoa, Samoan, Malo Sa'oloto — restricted; requires SIFA consent and a demonstrable connection or authorized use

Bank, Banking, Trust, Trustee, Assurance, Insurance, Reinsurance, Securities, Exchange, Clearing, Fund, Mutual Fund, Asset Management — requires prior licensing or consent of the Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) or the relevant financial services regulator
University, College, Institute, Academy, Chartered, Council, Association, Chamber of Commerce, Society — requires consent of the relevant professional or educational authority
Limited, Ltd, Incorporated, Corp, Public — restricted to approved liability suffixes; 'Limited' is the mandatory suffix for an International Company
Names identical or nearly identical to names already registered or reserved in the IC or domestic registers, and names likely to mislead as to the nature of the business
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name is notified in writing to the licensed agent with the statutory ground. Extension procedure: before expiry, the agent files an extension request with the continuation fee, renewing the reservation for a further period; a lapsed reservation releases the name for third-party use. Appeal SOP: (1) file a fresh name application where the conflict is referable to similarity; (2) within 14 business days of the rejection, the agent lodges a formal reconsideration submission to the Registrar of International Companies, with legal arguments and any consent letter from the Central Bank, ministry or professional authority; (3) if the Registrar maintains the refusal, an administrative review may be requested from the Samoa International Finance Authority Board; (4) a final judicial-review application may be filed with the Supreme Court of Samoa under the Judicature Ordinance 1961 and common-law administrative-law principles.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this industry: an International Company must at all times maintain a registered office and a licensed registered agent in Samoa under the International Companies Act 2017. The registered office may be the office of the licensed agent and need not be a physical trading premises of the company; the digital magazine portal may be operated entirely remotely with no Samoan employees or assets. However, SIFA economic-substance expectations for an IP-rich publishing and media vehicle require that core corporate decisions, minute books, accounting records and the shareholders' register remain documented and available at the registered agent's office in Samoa, and a suitable economic-substance statement should be maintained to avoid adverse OECD or global-tax-remediation findings.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for this risk tier: approximately 5-10% annual probability of an unannounced regulatory inspection of a standard low-risk digital publishing International Company; inspections are conducted primarily at the registered agent's premises against corporate records rather than at the company's foreign trading location. The probability rises to 20-30% where the vehicle exhibits IP-concentrated royalty flows, tax-exempt-status claims, nomination arrangements, or any STR or communications-data reporting trigger.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance — application for reservation of company name
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff (International Companies Regulations 2018 fee schedule)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certificate of Incorporation and initial registration of International Company
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: SIFA / Registrar of International Companies, Government of Samoa

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed registered agent and registered office — first year retainer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Samoa IC administration

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended, particularly sections 4 (Incorporation), 8 (Memorandum and Articles), and 19 (Registered Office and Agent).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation (issued pursuant to Form 1 – Application for Incorporation of an International Company).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement under the International Companies Act 1987; capital may be denominated in any currency and shares may be issued at par without immediate contribution. No escrow account requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (the “Company”), adopted on [Date]. 1. That the subscribers listed in the Memorandum of Association are hereby confirmed as the initial shareholders and that their respective share subscriptions are accepted as satisfactory. 2. That the registered office of the Company located at [Address], Apia, Samoa and the registered agent appointment are hereby ratified. 3. That [Name] be and is hereby appointed as President, [Name] as Secretary-Treasurer, and [Name] as Resident Agent, each to serve until their successors are elected. 4. That corporate banking signatories and online payment gateway accounts may be opened by the Secretary-Treasurer. 5. That the execution of digital publishing agreements is hereby authorized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request via the Registry’s online portal or in person, specifying the desired company name ending with 'Limited' or 'International'. Ensure the proposed name is not identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered entity. Pay the name reservation fee and obtain a written name clearance confirmation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Identity of the applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a written appeal with the Registrar within 14 days and resubmit an alternative name. The Registry may allow a post-clearance amendment on payment of a resubmission fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public and Registered Agent in Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, including the company name, registered office address, registered agent details, share structure, and permissible objects. The directors must sign the memorandum and articles, and signatures must be notarized. Submit the notarized documents to the International Companies Registry together with the prescribed statutory declaration of the registered agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry requires clarification, the registered agent may file a corrected instrument and re-executed statutory declarations within 7 days. Failure to cure defects within 30 days allows the Registry to return the application with a 50% refund of the filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Application and Pay Prescribed Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completion application via the Registry’s online submission portal or in person at the MCIL office in Apia. Attach the notarized memoranda, registered agent consents, and name clearance certificate. Pay the USD 250 statutory incorporation fee by bank draft or electronic transfer. The Registry will issue a stamped receipt.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for incomplete documents, the Registry will issue a compliance notice allowing 14 days to rectify. If the fee is underpaid, pay the difference within 5 business days or risk rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful vetting, the Registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation and assigns a company number. Download the certificate from the online portal or collect a hard copy from the Registry. The certificate is conclusive evidence of incorporation. Obtain the certified memorandum and articles for bank and commercial counterparts.
required_dossiers: Certified Copy of the Memorandum and Articles

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt First Board Resolutions and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; Corporate Services Provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a physical or virtual board meeting within 30 days of incorporation. Pass the first board resolutions as set out in the incorporation framework (share issuance, registered office, officers). Draft and retain board minutes, share register, register of directors, and registered agent consent in the company’s statutory records. Distribute share certificates to initial subscribers.
required_dossiers: Register of Members and Share Ledger

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – digital magazine publishing via online platform does not require an industrial license under Samoan law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) – Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – ICT/digital publishing activities are not listed under the 2007 Planning and Urban Management (Amendment) Act as requiring environmental registration or impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No direct industrial discharge, VOC, or wastewater streams applicable. Only standard electronic waste handling and good data-center housekeeping are recommended, aligned with the UK-style Waste Management Act standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate for registered office space if leased floor area exceeds 100 m2, structural integrity inspection from the Samoa National Building Authority for a standard office occupancy, and occupational health clearance from the Department of Labour regarding work-from-home and remote-worker arrangements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), successor to the Ministry for Revenue; administers the Tax Administration Act 2012, Income Tax Act 2012 and Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2002. Official portal and e-services: https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Samoa International Company (IC) must obtain its TIN through a licensed Registered Agent in Apia: (1) the agent files SRA TIN-01 taxpayer registration accompanied by the IC's Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar of International Companies (Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour), constitutional documents, director/shareholder register, registered agent address and AML/KYC due diligence; (2) SRA validates offshore status and issues a 10-digit TIN within 3-5 business days; (3) VAGST registration is required only if the IC makes taxable supplies exceeding WST 100,000 in any 12-month period, which does not apply to a pure offshore digital magazine exporter; (4) the TIN is mandatory to open a corporate bank account, receive Stripe/AdSense settlements through a Samoan licensed bank, and file annual compliance returns. No physical office in Samoa is required beyond the registered agent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — Samoa International Company is automatically exempt from Samoan income tax, corporate tax, dividend tax and royalty tax on foreign-source income, provided the IC does not trade with Samoan residents, own Samoan land, or carry on business in Samoa; exemption is statutory and requires no advance ruling.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or OECD hybrid-mismatch election exists in Samoa. Permitted elections include: (a) voluntary VAGST registration to recover input credits attributable to exported supplies; (b) an election under the International Companies Act to apply Companies Act governance provisions; and (c) an economic substance notification election evidencing that core income-generating activities are performed outside Samoa to preserve tax exemption. Samoa has not enacted domestic hybrid mismatch legislation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax) — consumption tax under the VAGST Act 2002, integrated with customs import VAT at the border.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 of taxable supplies in any consecutive 12-month period (mandatory threshold; voluntary registration permitted below threshold). A pure offshore IC supplying digital magazine subscriptions exclusively to non-residents has no Samoan taxable nexus and is not required to register.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None — Samoa does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, government API validation, e-invoicing clearance, or digital stamping. Electronic invoices (PDF/XML) are acceptable if they contain the statutory particulars under the VAGST Act 2002 (supplier name and TIN, issue date, sequential number, description, quantity, price, VAGST rate and amount, total). Records must be retained for at least 5 years; e-filing is available through the SRA portal without a clearance stamp.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to exported goods and exported services under the VAGST Act 2002. For the ISIC 5813 digital magazine portal: (i) the recipient must be a non-resident located outside Samoa at the time of supply; (ii) digital content is delivered and accessed outside Samoa; (iii) consideration is received in foreign currency via Stripe/AdSense payout rails; and (iv) no services are performed or enjoyed in Samoa and no Samoan resident subscribers are served. Supplies made to a Samoan resident are taxable at 15% and create a registration nexus.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic export entry via Samoa Customs Service using ASYCUDA World; for pure digital supplies a formal export register and exported-service declaration under the VAGST Act 2002 are substituted)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (required for physical goods; replaced by platform delivery logs and IP-geolocation evidence of access from outside Samoa for the digital magazine subscription service)
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by a licensed Samoa commercial bank evidencing foreign-currency inward remittance and FX repatriation within the 180-day deadline
Digital supply substantiation bundle: publisher export invoices, non-resident subscriber list, Stripe/AdSense payout settlement statements, and geolocation logs demonstrating off-Samoa consumption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The SRA cross-matches payment gateway settlement statements (Stripe/AdSense) against VAGST returns and bank IRCs during audit. Insufficient substantiation recharacterises the zero-rated supply as taxable at 15%, permitting retrospective reassessment within 5 years (10 years for fraud), penalty tax of up to 200% of the avoided tax for wilful false statements, late-payment interest at 2% per month compounding from the original due date, recovery of clawed-back input credits, criminal fines and imprisonment on conviction, deregistration of the IC, and potential personal liability for directors who certify false export documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa), exercising statutory powers under the Exchange Control Act 1976, Exchange Control Regulations 1976, Financial Institutions Act 1996, and Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007; enforcement of exchange-control directives is delegated to authorized dealers (licensed commercial banks).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is fully convertible for bona fide current-account transactions (trade, services, royalties, licensing fees) through authorized dealers provided the underlying documentation (invoice, contract, revenue statement) is presented; capital-account transactions and outward transfers exceeding prescribed reporting thresholds require prior Central Bank approval, and dividend/profit remittances to non-residents are liberally approved after verification of source-of-funds and tax-clearance records. International Companies under the International Companies Act 1987 are statutorily deemed non-residents for exchange-control purposes; consequently, USD/EUR-denominated shareholder capital, subscription revenue from non-resident platforms, and outbound disbursements to non-resident counterparties flow freely through a licensed foreign-currency account without Central Bank pre-clearance or mandatory conversion into WST. Practical limitation: no deep onshore WST/USD forward market exists and any physical WST transaction involving resident counterparties (local payroll, rent, utilities) will trigger standard exchange-control documentation requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For resident commercial exporters, export proceeds must be collected within 30 days of the contractual due date (or, in the absence of a due date, within 90 days of export shipment), remitted via an authorized dealer, and surrendered into WST no later than 30 days after receipt. International Companies operating a digital magazine portal are classified as non-resident entities: subscription, advertising (AdSense), and sponsored-media revenues received from Stripe/Google in USD/EUR into a designated foreign-currency account are outside the resident surrender regime and carry no conversion obligation. If, however, the International Company earns any revenue from Samoan residents or conducts business within Samoa, the resident exporter surrender rules would apply and require either Central Bank derogation or cessation of in-country business to preserve the non-resident standing.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited
Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility under strict conditions. An offshore digital EMI (Airwallex, Payoneer, Wise Business) is legally acceptable as a payment-collection and settlement intermediary, but it cannot function as the sole treasury account because Samoan AML enforcement and the Central Bank's guidance on correspondent banking require that material funds settle into a bank account licensed in Samoa. Recommended architecture: Stripe/AdSense payouts → EMI USD account (for platform where Samoa is not a direct payout jurisdiction) → periodic SWIFT USD wire to the BSP Samoa operational account; direct EMI-to-EMI disintermediation of the Samoan licensed bank is not acceptable for Stage 4 compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is generally mandatory for at least one director in person at the bank's premises in Apia, accompanied by the licensed Samoan Registered Agent, for the initial account opening interview; remote opening with a live video link is permitted on a discretionary, case-by-case basis when the client holds an existing performing banking relationship with a recognized foreign bank willing to issue an introducer letter, and provided the Registered Agent attends physically with corporate seal and certified board minutes. In all cases, banks require: original or notarized passports of all directors and the ultimate beneficial owner, certified Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum/Articles, Certificate of Good Standing from the International Companies Office, Registered Agent undertaking, and a board resolution resolving to open the specific account type.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume non-face-to-face revenue concentrated in only two global processors (Stripe and Google AdSense) without per-transaction customer identification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month platform payout history; list of all advertising partners and sponsored-media contracts; live content portfolio URLs; standard Terms of Service/refund policy; statutory declaration confirming no processing of Samoan Tala, no Samoan-resident customers, and no in-country business; external audit comfort letter covering revenue-flow reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO obscured by cascading trust/shareholder layers in a family-trust structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed UBO organizational chart; extract of the family trust deed or a written trustee confirmation; beneficial ownership declaration on the bank's prescribed form; foreign tax residence certificates for each beneficial owner; and a power-of-attorney authorizing the Registered Agent to disclose the trust register to the bank upon request.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Anticipated transaction velocity disproportionate to declared paid-up capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-statement evidence of minimum capital contribution equivalent to USD 50,000 into the Capital Escrow Account; projected 12-month cash-flow model tying revenue to platform analytics; purpose-of-account letter describing advertising license payments; commitment to supply monthly management accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered Agent / registered-office mismatch or past-due annual license renewal in the corporate registry
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Certificate of Good Standing; valid Registered Agent license certificate; a fresh board resolution ratifying the banking relationship; sworn confirmatory letter from the International Companies Office confirming no strike-off action pending.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/−PE filter flagged due to sub-licensees or freelance content contributors residing in high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-by-country list of all sub-licensees and material content contributors with ISO alpha-2 codes; negative-media and sanctions screening self-declaration; written commitment to notify the bank within five business days of any change in material counterparty nationality; standard contract clauses prohibiting sanctioned-party dealings.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial equity contribution shall be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's overseas account directly to the BSP Samoa USD Capital Escrow Account using purpose code '051 – Equity Injection / Capital Contribution' (or prevailing bank equivalent), with remittance information referencing the International Company registration number and the International Companies Act 1987. The bank must receive, prior to credit: signed board resolution, subscriber declaration form, UBO disclosure, and a source-of-wealth letter confirmed by the remitting bank. Enforcement note: because the entity is an International Company, the Samoa FIU does not require a CBS capital-import approval; however, funds arriving from a jurisdiction without credible AML standards are subject to a 5–10 business day hold and may be rejected absent the documentary bundle above. Alternative rail: Wise Business USD balance → local USD payout via SWIFT to BSP using the same purpose code; Stripe/AdSense-generated funds are not permitted to be the source of statutory capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement from the BSP Samoa operational account shall be executed by SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for correspondent rebalancing) via BSP's New York and Sydney correspondent banks, clearing through CHIPS/Fedwire for USD and RITS/Fedwire-equivalent for AUD; typical purpose codes include 'Royalties or License Fees', 'Professional Fees and Consulting', 'Data Processing and Hosting', and 'Advertising and Marketing'. For print-media procurement (magazine distribution contracts, paper and printing services) exceeding USD 5,000 per shipment, an irrevocable confirmed commercial letter of credit (SWIFT MT700, at-sight basis) shall be opened through BSP's trade-finance desk with a 5-day negotiation window and standard ICC UCP600 shipping documents. No local RTGS/CLS constraint applies because all material treasury flows are USD-denominated outside the WST settlement system; the IC does not require access to Samoa's national payment switch for its core digital publishing operations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable USD/WST forward contracts, tenor up to 12 months, available through BSP Samoa Treasury for the limited WST exposure arising from local registered-agent fees, legal retainers, and office services; fully collateralized by the positive USD operating balance; requires one-time CBS notification via the authorized dealer.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) in WST transacted offshore through an international counterparty (e.g., a top-tier global bank with a Far East booking centre) when the IC's indirect WST liability is estimated above USD 100,000 equivalent per quarter; settlement is in USD with no WST delivery, and CBS notification is satisfied by the authorized dealer's monthly foreign-exchange report.

Cross-currency swap (USD/EUR) for the periodic conversion of EUR-denominated subscription revenue (Stripe EUR settlements) into USD on a spot-plus-30-day sweep basis; permitted as a bespoke treasury product in Samoa, requires a formal bank credit approval and is subject to one-off CBS reporting, but is otherwise freely executable between a licensed Samoan bank and a non-resident IC.

Natural-hedge policy supplement: invoicing exclusively in USD, maintaining WST cash balances below USD 5,000 equivalent converted only once monthly at the interbank mid-rate, and contractual pass-through of permanent FX risk to advertising clients, thereby rendering the WST NDF execution materially unnecessary for the 12-month treasury horizon.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: International Company Annual Renewal and Government Fee Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) – Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on the anniversary of incorporation; a 30-day grace period applies from the anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs a WST 50 penalty; continued non-payment for 90 days beyond the anniversary date leads to administrative strike-off from the International Companies Register, with assets vesting in the Government of Samoa.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner and Statutory Register Confirmation to Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be completed within 30 days of each anniversary of incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the confirmation with the registered agent may result in the agent reporting the company to SIFA as non-compliant and, on notice, the company may be struck off after SIFA's compliance review.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Office and Registered Agent Renewal Affirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) – Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Combined with the annual renewal, due on the anniversary of incorporation with a 30-day grace period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the registered office or agent is not maintained or not affirmed, SIFA may issue a notice of non-compliance; failure to remedy within 60 days results in strike-off and dissolution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None. All Samoa International Companies, regardless of revenue, assets, or number of shareholders, are statutorily exempt from mandatory independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No mandatory framework; the International Companies Act requires accounting records sufficient to accurately explain transactions and financial position. IFRS may be adopted voluntarily.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each year, the registered agent must obtain written confirmation from the directors or shareholders identifying the current beneficial owner(s) and any transfers that occurred during the year. This confirmation is retained in the agent's AML/CFT file; it is not publicly filed.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$350 – US$1,200 per annum depending on service provider and level of regulatory support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable (no statutory audit). Voluntary review/compilation: US$1,500 – US$3,500

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% applicable to an International Company under the Samoa International Companies Act 1987; the standard domestic corporate income tax rate for resident companies is 25% under the Income Tax Act 2014
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full exemption from corporate income tax, withholding tax, capital gains tax, and stamp duty on all non-Samoa-source income and transactions of a duly licensed International Company; no annual income tax return is required; only the annual International Company government fee is payable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (Form 3) filed through the Samoa International Companies Registry e-Services portal administered by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour; no income tax return is filed for the tax-exempt International Company.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before 31 March each year in respect of the immediately preceding calendar year; newly incorporated International Companies must file within six months of incorporation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact registered company name, company number, date of incorporation, and registered office address in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the name as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation; non-resident beneficial owners need not be identified unless disclosed in the beneficial ownership register.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, licence number, and address of the Samoa-licensed resident agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An International Company cannot appoint itself as agent; the non-resident must maintain an approved resident agent for service of process and regulatory communications.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List of shareholders, classes of shares, number of shares held, and total issued share capital.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders may be listed; bearer shares are prohibited; nominee or trust holdings must be disclosed to the resident agent for AML purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, nationality, residential addresses, and appointment dates of all directors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors are permitted; at least one director may be an individual; details must be kept in the registered office but are not publicly filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement that the International Company has not carried on business in Samoa and has not derived Samoa-source income during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For digital magazine publishing, confirm the portal is operated wholly outside Samoa and that advertising and subscription revenue is derived from non-Samoa sources.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration by a director or the resident agent verifying that the information is true and correct.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This declaration must be signed by the resident agent or a director; knowingly false declarations expose the signatory to criminal penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a penalty of WST 100 per month or part month, capped at WST 1,000; late payment of the annual government fee attracts a 10% surcharge; persistent failure may lead to automatic strike-off, loss of legal personality, and a restoration fee plus all arrears.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for distributions made by an International Company; Samoa does not impose dividend withholding tax on International Company distributions, and the International Company is not a withholding agent for such payments.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No treaty relief is required for International Company dividend distributions because no Samoa withholding tax arises. Where a Samoa-source payment would nonetheless be characterized and a DTA applies, the non-resident beneficial owner must deliver to the payer: (1) a completed treaty relief declaration, (2) a valid Tax Residency Certificate from the residence country, and (3) a completed Samoa Form IR-COR before the payment date; the payer then applies the reduced treaty withholding rate and retains the documentation for tax audit purposes.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Under the Samoa Income Tax Act 2014, the statutory withholding rates on non-resident royalties and interest are 15% each, subject to DTA reductions. Under the Samoa–Australia and similar treaties, royalties and interest are generally reduced to 10%. For a tax-exempt International Company receiving or paying royalties and interest in connection with its foreign digital media business, no Samoan withholding tax applies because such income is not Samoa-source.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: WST 100,000 (administrative de minimis threshold for cross-border related-party transactions when a Samoa tax return is required; a tax-exempt International Company has no mandatory transfer pricing documentation obligation unless it is assessed as resident or subject to Samoa-source income).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Samoa International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations apply to International Companies carrying on relevant activities, including banking, insurance, fund management, financing or leasing, headquarters, shipping, and holding company activities. Digital magazine publishing and sponsored media placement do not constitute a relevant activity under the ESR. However, general anti-avoidance provisions and the sham transaction doctrine may disregard an International Company that has no commercial substance if it is interposed merely to divert advertising revenue away from the true economic operator.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion on undeclared Samoa-source revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a digital magazine portal with actual management, employees, servers, or advertising sales in Samoa, deriving Samoa-source gross revenue, and failing to register and file a resident company income tax return while falsely relying on International Company tax exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment on 100% of hidden taxable income plus a shortfall penalty of 200% of the evaded tax under the Samoa Income Tax Act 2014; daily penalties for failure to furnish a return; potential criminal fine up to WST 200,000 and imprisonment up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow directors are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties; courts may issue travel bans, freezing orders, disqualification orders, and sequestration of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Designation as a shell company without legitimate activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an International Company as a bare invoice conduit for digital advertisement sales, charging ad placement and sponsored media fees overseas while providing no staff, premises, contractual risk, or decision-making capacity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Samoa Revenue Division may apply general anti-avoidance rules to recharacterize revenue in the hands of the ultimate beneficial owner, impose back taxes with 200% penalties, and the Registrar may strike off the International Company for lacking economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly effect sham transactions may be personally liable for restitution, barred from serving as officers of any Samoa entity, and subject to criminal fines and imprisonment for false declarations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing Stripe or AdSense payouts through the International Company without maintaining a beneficial ownership register, transaction records, or customer due diligence files, and without reporting suspicious digital ad-revenue flows to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018, penalties include a fine of up to WST 1,000,000 and up to 14 years imprisonment; the resident agent may be suspended and the International Company deregistered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face criminal prosecution, personal asset freezing, travel bans, and disqualification from managing companies; civil liability may be imposed for losses suffered by third parties through the money-laundering conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly declaring that the International Company conducted no business in Samoa when, in fact, the digital magazine portal sold subscriptions, processed local payments, or placed advertisements for Samoa-based clients.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Companies Act 1987, knowingly making a false statement to the Registrar is an offence punishable by a fine of up to WST 10,000 and imprisonment for up to 7 years; the company also faces strike-off and restoration penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director or resident agent who signs the declaration bears personal criminal liability, including imprisonment, civil restitution to the Registrar and creditors, a travel ban pending trial, and deregistration of the entity.
